newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders steady.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb higher while feeder cattle were called steady, livestock analysts said.

Support in live cattle futures was expected to stem from apparent bottoming action in cash cattle prices. Packers were willing to pay $63 per cwt for cattle on Wednesday despite the falling boxed beef market. Some analysts also look for boxed values to bottom soon but others say weak beef will continue.
Boxed beef prices fell another $1.10 to $0.65 per cwt Wednesday with heavyweight choice beef falling to $98.53, the lowest level since February 20.
However, trading action in futures will likely be light as the market looks ahead to Friday's monthly Cattle-on-Feed report, they added.

Analyst estimates on the report put June 1 total on-feed cattle supplies in the major seven states at an average of 113.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 111.5 to 114 percent. A number at the high end would be a record high. Placement estimates averaged 117.2 percent in a range of 110.5 to 124 percent and marketings averaged 99 percent in a range of 97 to 100.5 percent.

Feeder cattle were called steady as expected with lower corn futures likely to offset the effects of a lower CME feeder cattle index. Cash feeders are showing near term weakness while the longer term trend is for tight supplies and expected strong fall markets, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.06 at $77.22 per cwt.
